paper_title: First Searches for Axions and Axion-Like Particles with the LUX Experiment
notes: Galactic ALP dark-matter search (axio-electric absorption), Fig. 7 red curve (LUX 2013, this work), 90% C.L. observed limit on g_Ae vs ALP mass over 1-16 keV/c^2. Mass axis converted keV/c^2 -> eV (x1000). Red LUX curve isolated by bright-red pixels (R>200,G<90,B<90), per-column median with error-bar caps averaging to central value; single outlier column removed. Extracted peak 4.2e-13 at ~13 keV matches the abstract quote (g_Ae no larger than 4.2e-13 across the full range); leftmost value ~8e-14 at 1 keV. Coupling already in canonical g_ae (dimensionless), no conversion needed. The paper also reports a separate mass-independent SOLAR axion limit g_Ae<3.5e-12 (Fig. 6, flat over 1e-5 to 1 keV) which is its abstract-leading headline; the galactic ALP DM curve was chosen here as the mass-dependent exclusion curve suited to the g_ae plane. DM density: paper assumes ALPs constitute all galactic dark matter but does not state a numerical local density (standard ~0.3 GeV/cm^3 implied); limit depends on density but value not given, so set null. Source figure is a raster JPG in the e-print (no ancillary data files).
